newsitem.title: GERMANY: THYSSEN DENIES RUMOURS ON E-PLUS.
newsitem.headline: THYSSEN DENIES RUMOURS ON E-PLUS.

text.p: Diversified steel maker Thyssen AG on Wednesday denied rumours it had reached agreement with utility Veba AG on selling Thyssen's share in their E-plus mobile telecommunications venture.

The rumours fueled a sharp rise in the price of Thyssen shares to 422 marks in afternoon electronic trade, though it dropped back to 415.25 marks by the close. Tuesday's electronic close was 401.10 marks
A Thyssen spokesman said there was no agreement on E-plus's future, as the two sides have widely divergent views on the appropriate price for E-plus.
Thyssen and Veba, which each hold 31.25 percent of E-plus have been discussing the sale for a long time. BellSouth Corp of the U.S. is the third major shareholder with a 22.5 percent stake.
Thyssen has said it is not under time pressure to reach a decision, and could hold on to the E-plus stake in view of increasing growth by the network.
